title: Pin safeguard orchestration and deprecation quiesce for region-aware model serving
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Customers pin model versions to guarantee deterministic behavior, but pins currently block safe deprecation and regional scaling strategies. When a pinned model becomes deprecated (end-of-life, security advisory, or unsupported quantization), our current options are either a blunt forced-unpin (high customer impact) or best-effort manual coordination with customers (expensive and slow). We need a system that preserves customer expectations for pinned versions while enabling graceful, observable, and automatable transitions across regions and model variants.

Goal:
Design and implement a Pin Safeguard Orchestration (PSO) subsystem that: 
- Prevents silent breaking changes for pinned versions while allowing safe, low-impact deprecation flows.
- Supports region-aware degrade paths (regional variant promotion) and model-variant substitutions with explicit compatibility scoring.
- Publishes a machine-readable performance profile for each pinned version and a deprecation quiesce window that the control plane can act on.
- Integrates with Console notifications, alerting, and rollout primitives (canaries, forced-fallback windows).

Key concepts and proposed controls:
1) Pin TTL and Immutable Grace Periods: pins have metadata fields (created_at, owner, ttl, immutable_until). By default pins are immutable for 30 days. Admins can propose a pin-expiry with an enforced notification cadence.
2) Compatibility Score: each model-version publish includes a list of compatible variants and a numeric compatibility_score (0-100) derived from performance-profile checks (latency, RMSE on eval prompts, output schema checks). The PSO uses thresholds to decide allowable automatic substitutions.
3) Regional Promote/Degrade Policy: policies can be defined per-customer or org-wide to prefer regional-compatible variants before cross-region routing. E.g., if eu-west variant is unhealthy for a pinned model, prefer eu-west-quantized variant with compatibility_score >= 85 before routing to us-west.
4) Deprecation Quiesce Window: a deprecation announcement creates a quiesce window with three phases: Announce (communication + read-only telemetry), Canary (traffic split with opt-in autofallback after N failures), and Forced-Fallback Window (only after exhausting reconciliation and with mandatory customer notification).
5) Safety Escalation: automated rollback rules that escalate to on-call and require explicit engineering override if compatibility_score drops below 60 for >= 5m for >10% of p99 latency.

Acceptance criteria:
- PSO can evaluate and execute a regional degrade in staging and produce an audit trail in Console.
- Publish performance profiles for pinned versions to the model catalog UI and expose compatibility_score through the API.
- Integrate notification emails and console banners for 30/14/7/1 day pre-deprecation reminders.
- Provide a migration API endpoint /pins/:key/suggest-migrations that returns ranked variant suggestions with reasons and expected delta on latency/cost.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Full enterprise legal workflow for forced deprecations (handled in a separate enterprise-compliance ticket).
- On-prem installation automation (will be follow-up after core PSO behavior is validated).
acceptance_criteria: Staging demo: execute a regional degrade for a pinned model and show traffic split telemetry in Console
API: GET /models/:id/versions/:v/perf-profile returns JSON (published) and includes compatibility_score
Notifications: 30/14/7/1 day pre-deprecation messages appear in Console and create an email event
Audit: every automatic substitution writes an immutable audit record with reason and metrics snapshot
comments: 2025-02-13 — Triage: Identified as customer-impacting for customers who pin long-lived versions. Assigned to Marcus. (Aisha)
2025-02-18 — Architecture sync: Proposed compatibility_score computed from 50% eval-match, 30% latency headroom, 20% schema/safety checks. Marcus to prototype scoring function. (Marcus, Elena)
2025-02-24 — Design review: PM and Design approved the Console banner copy and notification cadence. Link to design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PSO/Design (DES-3121) (Sophie)

2025-02-27 — Implementation kickoff: Created prototype PR for perf-profile schema and catalog changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7892 (WIP). Added initial API routes. (Marcus)
2025-03-03 — Blocker: Need decision on default immutable_until duration (30d vs 14d). Security asked for 30d; Growth suggested 14d for faster UX. Set to 30d for initial release. (PM: Viktor)
2025-03-05 — Infra note: Autoscaler needs a signal hook (compatibility_score < 70) to avoid batching into incompatible kernels. Ticket opened: ENG-26201. (Infra: Lina)
implementation_notes: Prototype approach: attach perf-profile objects to model-version metadata in the catalog. A scoring lambda runs every publish or on-demand. Runtime subscribes to an allowlist of substitutions per-org. Console shows suggested migration and 'apply fallback' button which calls the rollout service. Audit log format follows existing rollout-audit schema. Ensure KV-cache compatibility checks are included in the scoring to avoid silent correctness regressions.

Console: implement migration suggestions panel and notification banner (DES & PM)
